result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B picks Georgia, which ships on Mac, Windows and iOS, and says plainly what Android falls back to. It also catches that Georgia's old-style numerals are a problem on invoices, and gives specific checks for metric differences across platforms. A leads with Iowan Old Style, which only Mac and iOS have, so most Windows users see Palatino instead. A's reasons for the pairing are thinner, and it calls licensing moot instead of naming what to upgrade to once licensing is cleared. B doesn't do that either: its only upgrade suggestion is other system fonts. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A picks Georgia, which looks much the same on Mac, Windows and iOS, and pairs it with the system sans. It also explains why the pairing suits law firms and flags a real billing pitfall: Georgia's old-style numerals make invoice amounts hard to scan. B's lead face, Iowan Old Style, exists only on Mac and iOS, so Windows and Android users will see a different heading font, and B dismisses licensing as moot without saying what to upgrade later. Neither answer clearly lays out a web-font upgrade for when legal clears licenses.
